findings.title: Use git ls-tree --full-tree --name-only <commit> .ai/tasks/ (trailing slash), take basenames and match TASK pattern exactly
De-duplicate commit OIDs before one ls-tree per commit; latency grows with refs
Specify the git failure code and test that no task directory is created when collection fails
Treeless partial clones may lazily fetch during ls-tree; consider GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1
Test empty ref sets and refs without .ai/tasks as non-errors

summary: Design is correct and scoped: git collection stays in git_context/task_service and reserve_task_id only takes extra numbers as a floor, keeping the mkdir retry loop. Failing closed is safe because start already requires a git context, start --recover never reserves IDs, and repositories without other refs return empty output. Per-commit ls-tree costs about 1.25 s for 36 unique commits here; acceptable. Conditions for implementation: exact ls-tree form with trailing slash and --full-tree, and a specified git failure code with a test that no task directory is created on failure.
